locus: Theses in quibus exponitur Doctrina Scholae Romanae circa partitionem Gratiae in sufficientem atque efficacem, & concordiam libertatis humanae cum Gratiae efficacia, LXXIII-LXXXIX (Thomists and Jansenius agree that grace is efficacious of itself and determines the will physically; they differ on its nature (Alvarez's virtual motion received passively against Jansenius's vital act of love; De gratia Christi Salvatoris 8.1), on absolute premotion against relative delight, on the reason it is needed (dependence of second causes against the wound of sin), and on the state of innocence (adjutorium sine quo); Molina's contrary doctrine (Concordia, question 14, article 13, disputations 12, 37, 40; question 23, articles 4-5): sufficient aid given to all, divided into efficacious and inefficacious by its outcome, efficacy from free consent even in the composite sense, more grace may convert no one, the consent supernatural through cooperating grace as the Spirit's instrument, two anathemas, grace and free choice as two parts of one complete cause).
